executive_summary: USD/CHF closed at 0.8288 on 2026-10-02 in the gated price store. That is 1 Swiss franc per dollar times 0.8288, so a rising pair means a stronger dollar and a weaker franc. The pair is up 2.62% over one month, 2.51% over three months, 4.84% over six months and 4.02% over one year, and its close sits at the 90th percentile of the 52-week close range. The story is a single number: a 387.5bp gap between the Fed's policy rate and the SNB's zero rate. The futures roll widens that to an executable 453.6bp, and it is propped up by a roughly 260bp gap in core inflation. The SNB does not meet before 2026-12-10, so no scheduled event inside four weeks can narrow the gap. The pair-level view adds two things the single-currency dossiers do not show. First, the dollar's strategic problem (peers still raising rates while the Fed's projections are flat) does not apply against the franc, because Switzerland is the one G10 economy that is not tightening. Second, speculators are long the dollar and short the franc at the same time, and the trade is being routed through this exact pair, which concentrates the crowding risk here. The settled verdict is Bullish tactically (conviction 3, score +0.3833) and Bullish strategically (conviction 2, score +0.1122). I use a 2–4 week target of 0.8400 and a six-month target of 0.8450. The six-month target sits where the declining 200-week average and the top of the five-touch 0.8375–0.8456 resistance band converge. The caveat is serious. After the valuation date, September payrolls printed +29,000 against 90,000 expected, with August revised to 133,000. The French-German 10-year spread temporarily widened beyond 150 basis points, its highest since November 2011. The pair also printed a bearish outside-day reversal on 2026-10-01. The tactical case is therefore weaker today than its score implies.

market_context.recent_regime: The pair has been a pure rate-differential trade. It moved up after the Fed's 2026-09-16 hike: the SNB is widely expected to keep its benchmark rate at 0% well into 2027. The seven-session run that followed was driven by Fed hike odds and Treasury yields above 5%, in a calm tape that gave the franc no safe-haven bid. That regime was tested in the two sessions after the valuation date. US data softened: CME FedWatch participants assigned roughly a 28% probability to an October hike by 2026-10-02. At the same time, French sovereign stress began routing European capital into francs. The dominant narrative is still carry, but for the first time this quarter its two pillars (a hawkish Fed and a calm Europe) are being questioned in the same week. The rally came in two legs: from the 2026-08-19 close of 0.79725 to the 2026-09-16 Fed-hike close of 0.82594, and a seven-session run from 0.82056 on 2026-09-22 to 0.83581 on 2026-09-30.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral policy differential is +387.5bp in the dollar's favour on the Fed effective midpoint of 3.875 per cent against an SNB policy rate of exactly zero, which the gated payload confirms as policyDifferential 3.875. This is the widest gap the dollar carries against any G10 currency and it is the pair's primary driver. The executable cost is wider still: the CME calendar-spread roll prices a long franc position at minus 453.6bp annualised, roughly 66bp beyond the policy spread, with the wedge being interest differential plus cross-currency basis that cannot be separated without an OIS curve. At the long end the live prints in the two dossiers put Treasuries near 5.24 per cent against Swiss ten-year paper near 0.58 per cent, about 466bp, and that gap widened by roughly 36bp through September as US ten-year yields rose 51bp against 15bp in Switzerland; the payload's own 4.21 percentage point long-end differential is an August monthly vintage and is not quoted here as a live level. The decisive tactical asymmetry is calendar rather than level: the gated meeting file shows one FOMC on 2026-10-28 inside the four-week window and no SNB decision at all until 2026-12-10, so on scheduled events the differential can only widen or hold, never narrow. Transmission is straightforward carry plus the real-yield channel, with a franc that pays nothing acting as the funding leg of the trade the dollar's yield attracts.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the question is the direction of the differential, and here the pair is the exception to the dollar's general strategic problem. The dollar dossier turns Policy and Rates to Neutral strategically because the ECB, BoJ, BoE, RBA and Norges Bank are all still tightening while the Fed's dots are flat at 4.1 per cent through 2027 — but Switzerland is the one peer that is not in that group. The SNB's own conditional inflation forecast of 0.7, 0.8 and 0.8 per cent for 2026 to 2028 is constructed explicitly on an unchanged zero rate, and ING and OCBC both publish an SNB on hold through 2027. If the Fed delivers the hike its September projections imply at the 2026-12-09 SEP meeting and the SNB holds the following day on 2026-12-10, the bilateral gap widens to 412.5bp; the Fed then plateaus, so the widening stops, but the franc has no mechanism to close it. The counterweight is pricing rather than policy: the Swiss curve already embeds roughly 75bp of SNB tightening by September 2027, so a franc-holder's measured forward disadvantage narrows mechanically even if the SNB never moves, and the market's own 50 per cent probability on 2026-12-10 is the single largest binary in this verdict. Confidence falls from 70 to 62 for that reason, not because the level of carry decays.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The inflation differential is the mechanism and the growth differential is the complication. US core PCE ran 3.0 per cent year on year in August with headline at 3.4 per cent, against Swiss core at 0.4 per cent — the lowest in the G10 plus Singapore set — and Swiss headline at 0.8 per cent, a gap of roughly 260bp on the core measures that fixes the Fed in a tightening posture and the SNB in a dormant one. The energy shock that produced the global impulse barely touches Switzerland because energy is about 3.5 per cent of the Swiss basket against roughly 7 per cent in the euro area, and the United States is a net energy exporter whose terms of trade improve on the same shock. Against that, the growth differential currently favours the quote currency, not the base: Swiss Q2 GDP grew 1.885 per cent quarter on quarter and 2.63 per cent year on year against US 2.1 per cent year on year, and the KOF barometer printed a five-year high of 109.1. That matters less than it looks because Swiss nominal wage growth is 0.4 per cent, so output growth is not generating income growth or domestic inflation, and SECO itself attributes about half of Q2 to the volatile chemical and pharmaceutical sector. The honest tactical qualification is the Swiss September CPI released on the morning of the valuation date at 1.0 per cent headline, above the 0.8 per cent base, which lifts rather than undercuts December SNB hike pricing; confidence is set at 55 rather than 62 for that reason.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the inflation gap outlasts the growth gap. The Fed's own projections take headline PCE from 3.7 per cent in 2026 to 2.3 per cent in 2027 and core from 3.4 to 2.5 per cent, which still leaves US core roughly 200bp above a Swiss core of 0.4 per cent and a SECO panel forecast of 0.6 per cent average Swiss inflation for both 2026 and 2027. A 200bp inflation differential is the structural reason the two policy rates sit 387.5bp apart, and nothing in either forecast closes it inside the horizon. The growth side converges rather than diverges: SECO expects a Swiss second-half slowdown after a pharma-flattered Q2 and left 2027 at 1.6 per cent, while US GDPNow has already fallen from 5.1 to 3.7 per cent and US consumer confidence is weak at 81.9 with a 4.1 per cent saving rate. The net is a factor that supports the pair through the policy channel while offering no additional growth premium, which is a Bullish 55 rather than a Bullish 65. The risk that matters is a second Swiss headline print above 1.0 per cent, which would make the market's SNB hike pricing a forecast rather than a misreading and would hit the pair through the Swiss front end.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The current tape is the specific configuration in which the dollar leg wins and the franc leg gets nothing. VIX closed near 16 at the 34th percentile of its one-year range, the S&P 500 is up roughly 12 to 14 per cent year to date and within two per cent of its record, and investment-grade spreads at 83bp are historically tight — an environment with no capital flight, which is the only mechanism by which the franc overrides a 387.5bp carry disadvantage. The dollar meanwhile sits on the right-hand side of the smile, supported by exceptionalism and a 2.88 per cent ten-year real yield rather than by fear. The corroboration is gold, which is the franc's only genuine commodity link and runs through shared haven demand rather than trade: gold fell about six per cent over the month while the dollar index rose, and the dollar's sixty-day correlation to gold is minus 0.53, so the same signal shows up twice. The two counterweights are credit and France — US high-yield spreads widened 59bp to 324bp at the 98th percentile of their one-year range, and the OAT-Bund spread at 111.2bp is at a one-year high with a large French budget vote pending, which is the live channel through which European sovereign stress routes capital into francs rather than euros. On balance the equity and volatility channels dominate the credit and sovereign channels over four weeks.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the risk factor becomes genuinely two-sided for this pair in a way it is not for an ordinary dollar cross, because both legs are havens with different triggers. A euro-area sovereign accident out of France, or a Gulf escalation that re-closes Hormuz, would bid the franc through repatriation and the dollar through funding, and which leg wins depends on whether the shock is a credit event or a dollar-liquidity event — the dollar wins the latter, the franc tends to win the former. A Gulf settlement, which the dollar dossier puts at 25 per cent over six months, is doubly negative for the franc because it removes both the haven bid and the energy-driven inflation impulse behind SNB hike pricing, but it is also negative for the dollar because it removes the US terms-of-trade gain and pulls headline inflation down. These are not symmetric in magnitude but they are symmetric enough in sign that no directional claim survives. The second consideration is convexity: the franc's return distribution is low-volatility in the body and extremely fat in the tail, with the January 2015 floor removal as the reference, so a short-franc exposure held for three months is implicitly short a cheap option. Neutral at 50 is the honest reading of a wide, roughly balanced distribution.

Speculators are long the dollar and short the franc at the same time, which amplifies rather than mutes the pair signal: the IMM aggregate dollar long rose 12.5 billion dollars in a single week to 18.4 billion, the fastest weekly build in seven years, while leveraged funds carried a franc net short of 16,457 contracts at minus 12.3 per cent of open interest, the most stretched reading in the cached sample, after five consecutive weeks of building. Crucially, the crowding is pair-specific rather than generic, because ING describes this exact pair as a popular vehicle for expressing hawkish Fed views and Reuters documents an active rotation of carry funding out of the yen into the franc after Japanese intervention. That is two independent flows pointed at one cross. Against that, the dollar leg is only at the 44th percentile of its own cached range, so the trade is crowded through the franc rather than through the dollar, and the franc all-speculator net has already trimmed from minus 30,000 to minus 26,800 without producing a rally, meaning some of the squeeze fuel has been spent. tactical.bilateral_analysis: The external differential between these two economies is the widest in the G10 and it transmits on a timescale far longer than four weeks. Switzerland runs a current account surplus of 9.198 per cent of GDP with a net international investment position of 986bn francs; the United States runs a deficit of 3.0 per cent of GDP with a net international investment position of minus 22.42 trillion dollars — a gap of over 12 percentage points of GDP in the franc's favour. The bilateral trade relationship points the same way: IMF DOTS shows Swiss goods exports to the United States of 73.5bn dollars against imports of 29.3bn, and a US net goods deficit with Switzerland of 38.6bn, so the direct trade flow is a structural franc bid. None of that generates identifiable transaction demand inside a four-week window, and two short-horizon offsets work the other way: the United States is a net energy exporter benefiting from Brent near 100 dollars while Switzerland imports energy, and the high-frequency Swiss monthly trade balance narrowed to 3.786bn francs from 5.742bn. Note also that the Swiss export mix is 39.9 per cent precious metals, so monthly Swiss trade data carries a large non-economic gold-transit component and should not be read as a clean flow signal. Neutral at 55.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a 0.16 weight this is the strongest structural argument against the pair and the only materially negative line in the strategic score. Valuation does not contradict the view but it does limit it — the franc's real effective rate at 99.87 is 2.83 per cent lower year on year and at roughly the 42nd percentile of its post-2020 range, so this is a cheapening currency rather than an expensive one being corrected, which means the surplus caps the pair rather than reversing it. net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: USD: net energy exporter. Oil up is a mild to moderate dollar positive through terms of trade and through the headline inflation channel that keeps the Fed hawkish (WTI 96.16, Brent near 100 to 103, up roughly 50 to 56 per cent year on year). Gold up is a dollar negative — the sixty-day dollar index to gold correlation is minus 0.53.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: CHF: no direct commodity export exposure at all. The franc's only commodity link is gold, and it runs through shared safe-haven demand rather than trade (gold up is CHF positive). Switzerland is a net energy importer, but energy is only about 3.5 per cent of the CPI basket, so the oil sensitivity is small. Precious metals are 39.9 per cent of Swiss goods exports, which is transit and refining rather than resource rent.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Applying the framework's direction rules bilaterally. Oil up: base gets a clear positive (US net energy exporter, plus the hawkish inflation impulse); quote gets a small negative (energy importer, but only 3.5 per cent of the basket, and a plateaued impulse that lifted Swiss headline only to 0.8 per cent). Net of a strong positive against a small negative, the pair RISES on higher oil — bullish USD/CHF, though the magnitude is modest because the Swiss leg barely responds. Gold up: base gets a clear negative (minus 0.53 correlation), quote gets a positive through shared haven demand. Net, the pair FALLS on higher gold — and this is the larger of the two sensitivities because it hits both legs in the same direction rather than in opposite proportions. The observed month confirms the netting: gold fell about six per cent while the pair rose, which is both legs of the gold channel firing together.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Pair rises modestly, roughly 0.3 to 0.6 per cent. The US terms-of-trade gain and the resulting support for a December Fed hike outweigh a Swiss import cost that barely registers in a 3.5 per cent energy weight. The second-order risk runs the other way: a large enough oil spike would lift Swiss headline CPI toward 1.2 per cent and revive SNB hike pricing, which is the channel through which the energy trade eventually turns against the pair.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Pair falls modestly, roughly 0.3 to 0.5 per cent, but with an important offset: lower oil also collapses the Swiss headline inflation impulse and therefore the market's SNB hike pricing, which is franc-negative. A Gulf settlement is the cleanest version of this and is close to a wash for the pair even though it is clearly negative for the dollar in isolation.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: Gold, not oil. It is the only commodity that moves both legs of this pair in the same direction simultaneously — negative for the dollar on a minus 0.53 correlation and positive for the franc through shared haven demand — so a gold rally is the single most reliable commodity signal that the pair is about to fall.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Guidance diverges about as sharply as two credible central banks can manage. The Fed hiked 12-0 on 2026-09-16, replaced conditional language with a commitment to deliver price stability, published a dot distribution in which 12 of 18 participants see another move by December, and did so against explicit political pressure — which, with the Supreme Court having barred removal of a governor without cause, reads as institutional independence reaffirmed. The SNB by contrast gives minimal forward guidance by design, meets four times a year, and published a conditional forecast of 0.7, 0.8 and 0.8 per cent built on the assumption that the rate stays at zero. The one language change in September was franc-negative: the June formulation about an increased willingness to intervene was dropped back to the standard wording, which is a central bank signalling comfort with a weaker currency. The communication regime asymmetry is the tactical mechanism: the Fed has the 2026-10-07 minutes and the 2026-10-28 decision inside the window, while the SNB has nothing at all until 2026-12-10, so all the guidance flow in the next four weeks comes from the leg that is hawkish. A bank with no scheduled microphone cannot talk its currency up.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a 0.12 strategic weight this factor turns on one meeting pair, and the sequence matters: the FOMC publishes projections on 2026-12-09 and the SNB publishes its quarterly assessment and conditional inflation forecast the very next day, 2026-12-10. The Fed therefore sets the tone and the SNB responds into it, which historically amplifies rather than dampens the divergence. Three outcomes are distinguishable. If the Fed delivers and the SNB holds with another forecast built on zero — our base case — the roughly 75bp of Swiss tightening embedded in the front end becomes hard to sustain and the pair is supported by the repricing alone. If the SNB holds but references normalisation or lifts its 2027 forecast, the market's pricing is validated and the pair falls sharply. If the SNB hikes, the largest single input in this verdict is wrong. Credibility cuts both ways and roughly cancels: the Fed's record keeps breakevens anchored at 2.36 per cent despite 3.4 per cent headline PCE, while the SNB has the best inflation record in the developed world and its forecasts deserve to be believed over the curve — which is itself the franc-negative reading. Confidence 55 rather than 62 because a coin flip the market itself prices at 50 per cent cannot support a stronger claim.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Event risk over four weeks is dense but the tails offset for this cross specifically. On the base leg the dated items are the FOMC minutes on 2026-10-07, US CPI on 2026-10-14, the 2026-10-28 decision and the 2026-11-03 midterms just beyond the window. On the quote leg there is no Swiss domestic political risk worth pricing — a stable federal government, no election inside the horizon, and the EU Bilaterals III package not due to enter force before end-2028 — so the franc's event exposure is entirely imported. The two imported binaries are the French budget vote in the second week of October, which is franc-positive through the eurozone-stress haven channel with OAT-Bund already at a one-year high of 111.2bp, and the Iran negotiation at day 215, where a failure lifts both legs and a settlement hurts both legs. The netting is genuinely balanced: a French accident pushes the pair down, a Gulf escalation pushes both currencies up with an ambiguous net, a Gulf settlement removes the US terms-of-trade gain and the franc's haven bid simultaneously, and a US shutdown risk is outside the window. Options are not charging much for any of it — one-month implied of 7.114 per cent against twenty-day realised of 5.25 per cent is a premium for an event nobody has named.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the event calendar skews against the pair, and it does so because the base leg carries almost all of the dated risk. tactical.bilateral_analysis: The sovereign quality differential in this pair is the widest in the G10, but it is not a four-week driver. The United States is rated AA plus by S&P and Fitch and Aa1 by Moody's, carries debt held by the public at 101 per cent of GDP, a federal deficit near 6 per cent and net interest above one trillion dollars or 3.3 per cent of GDP; Switzerland is AAA or Aaa at all five agencies with a balanced federal budget, a constitutional debt brake, general government gross debt of 38.5 per cent of GDP falling toward 33.5 per cent by 2031, and a ten-year yield of 0.58 per cent that contains no identifiable credit premium. That is roughly 62 percentage points of debt-to-GDP and two to three notches of rating in the quote currency's favour. It does not move the pair now because higher US yields have attracted rather than repelled capital — July TIC inflows were 83.7bn dollars — so fiscal deterioration is being priced in the term premium rather than in the currency. No dated fiscal event falls inside the tactical window; the 2026-12-11 funding deadline is outside it. Neutral at 55.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At one to three months fiscal gravity starts to apply, and this is one of the few pairs where the sovereign differential is large enough to matter on its own. US net interest already exceeds defence spending at 3.3 per cent of GDP, the deficit runs near 6 per cent at full employment leaving no counter-cyclical room, and tariff revenue that was meant to offset part of it is shrinking after the IEEPA ruling and the expiry of Section 122. The dated catalyst is the 2026-12-11 funding deadline, which falls at the year-end turn and one day after the SNB meets; Fitch explicitly cited gridlock and shutdown risk when affirming AA plus. The Swiss side offers no counterweight in the other direction — it simply does not deteriorate, and its consolidation path is a constitutional rule rather than a forecast. The transmission mechanism to the pair is the point at which higher US yields stop attracting capital and start demanding a currency risk premium; that link has not broken yet, which is why confidence is 58 rather than 70, but the direction of travel over this horizon is one-way. Care is taken not to double-count the haven channel, which belongs in Factors 3 and 7.

The 25-delta risk reversal deepens from minus 0.238 at 99.7 days to minus 0.485 at 190.6 days and the butterfly widens from 0.206 to 0.280, so the options market is paying progressively more for downside and for wings as the horizon extends — the pattern of participants who want the carry but do not trust it to survive a quarter. That contradiction is reported rather than resolved, and the aggregator figure is not treated as bank research. Pass-2 level addendum: short-horizon bank views are now cautious on levels. UOB's Quek Ser Leang notes USD/CHF reversed sharply from 0.8382 to close at 0.8286; over 1–3 months he still anticipates a rebound, though not strong enough to revisit the July peak (UOB 1–3 week range 0.8245–0.8365). The bank flows that built the trade remain in place: Rabobank raised its nine- to 12-month EUR/CHF forecast to 0.95 from 0.94, and BofA's Adarsh Sinha notes Swiss rates are lower than Japan's and franc volatility is lower as well. The market is not buying the SNB's guidance: the SNB pushed back against market expectations of 50 to 75bp of hikes over the next 12 months, yet OIS pricing points to more than two SNB rate hikes by mid-next year. Statistical and retail forecasts disagree with each other: one model puts USD/CHF between 0.7923 and 0.8247 by December 2026, below spot. The analyst's 0.8400 / 0.8450 targets sit above that and below the technical-model ranges that extend to 0.8580.
consensus_divergence.bank_consensus_forecast_source: OCBC, ING, BofA, Rabobank and UOB research commentary (directional views only; no bank point forecast for USD/CHF located). Exchange Rates UK aggregator survey noted separately and not treated as bank research.
consensus_divergence.our_tactical_view: Bullish the pair at conviction 3 on a net score of plus 0.3833, driven by a 387.5bp differential that no scheduled event inside the window can narrow.
consensus_divergence.our_strategic_view: Bullish the pair at conviction 2 on a net score of plus 0.1122 — a carry-carried view with a large structural offset, not a trend call.
consensus_divergence.divergence_direction: In line with bank commentary on direction (OCBC, ING, BofA, Rabobank and UOB are all franc-negative) and against the aggregator survey, which leans toward a softer pair. On conviction we are below the bank commentary strategically, because the structural external and fiscal differentials take back most of the carry.
consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: Not quantifiable in pips — no bank numeric point forecast located; strategic conviction (2) is below the bank commentary's implied conviction.
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Two bilateral factors are weighted differently from the commentary. First, the external balance: the bank narrative treats the franc purely as a funding currency and prices a Swiss current account surplus of 9.198 per cent of GDP, a net international investment position of plus 986bn francs and a bilateral goods surplus with the United States of 38.6bn dollars at zero, which is defensible over weeks and not over quarters — the surplus caps the pair even when it cannot reverse it. Second, the sequencing of the December decisions: the consensus treats an SNB hold as neutral when it is in fact franc-negative, because the Swiss front end has added 19bp on the opposite assumption, and treats a Fed hike as settled when the base currency simultaneously faces a funding cliff on 2026-12-11 and a midterm election. We therefore accept the carry argument tactically and discount it strategically.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: Tactically the view is paid twice — by the differential at roughly 26 pips a month and by a repricing of the Swiss front end as December SNB hike odds decay with no scheduled Swiss communication to support them. Strategically the payoff is mostly carry rather than spot, which is the honest characterisation of a plus 0.1122 score.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: The single largest error term is the SNB on 2026-12-10. If it hikes or references normalisation, the largest input in this verdict inverts and a concentrated franc short covers into open interest that has already fallen 22.1 per cent. The secondary risks are a soft US data print that removes the December hike, which takes the base leg's support away without the franc improving, and a French or Gulf shock that bids the franc faster than the dollar.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: Both horizons are Bullish for the pair, but the strength decays by two thirds and the composition changes completely. The tactical score is built on agreement, with five Bullish factors and a single opposing contribution of minus 0.0550; the strategic score is a residual, with nearly two thirds of its positive weight in one factor and four Bearish factors taking most of it back. The mechanism is the weight migration: External Balance rises from 0.06 to 0.16 and Fiscal from 0.04 to 0.07, so the widest current account gap and the widest sovereign quality gap in the G10 acquire real weight exactly as the data-flow factors lose it. The direction survives only because Switzerland is the one G10 peer not tightening into the Fed's plateau, which is what keeps Policy and Rates Bullish here when the base dossier has it Neutral everywhere else.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: The 2026-12-09 FOMC with projections and the 2026-12-10 SNB assessment, falling on consecutive days, with the US funding deadline on 2026-12-11 immediately after. That three-day cluster is where the carry differential is either widened to 412.5bp and confirmed, or where the SNB validates the market's hike pricing and the thesis inverts.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Treat the two horizons as the same direction held with different conviction and different instruments. The tactical view is the high-conviction one and the carry pays while it is held; the strategic view is a carry hold with a structural brake and a crowded position behind it, and the deepening six-month risk reversal argues for carrying it with protection rather than outright. The second pass should note that the three-day December cluster is not priced as an event in the vol term structure, which is flat across it. Pass-2 implementation: run the tactical long from 0.8235–0.8290 with a 0.8140 stop into the 2026-10-28 FOMC, and take partial profits at 0.8384. Roll the remainder into the strategic carry hold only if the pair is above 0.8184 after the FOMC. Add strategic exposure on dips to 0.8160–0.8250 with option protection bought before the December cluster, since the term structure is not charging for it.

catalysts.rationale: Payrolls rose 29,000 against 90,000 expected, with August revised to 133,000. That fires the payroll unwind trigger in Factor 4 and the USD dossier. It removes most of the October hike premium and is why the pair fell to 0.82308 before closing at 0.8288.

catalysts.event: FOMC minutes of the 15–16 September meeting
catalysts.rationale: The minutes reveal how broad the hawkish majority was behind a 12-0 hike with 12 of 18 dots showing another move. The SNB has no communication until 2026-12-10, so every unit of policy information in this window moves the base leg only. After the payroll miss, a hawkish set of minutes is the first chance to rebuild December pricing.

Both legs of the speculative position point the same way, so the weekly print is a bilateral signal. A narrowing of the −12.3%-of-open-interest franc short alongside a pair below 0.8235 would confirm the covering move. A rebuilt short above 0.8300 would show the carry bid has re-asserted itself.

catalysts.event: French National Assembly vote on the €54bn budget (week of 2026-10-12; no published date located)
catalysts.rationale: This is the cleanest franc-positive catalyst and it is already active. The franc is being supported by capital outflows from French assets. A government collapse routes European capital into francs, not euros, and takes the pair down through a quote-leg haven bid rather than any dollar weakness.

The decisive tactical print. Core at or above 0.3% m/m restores the December hike that the pair's rate support rests on. Core at or below 0.1% confirms the payroll message and triggers the tactical Decrease-to-2 condition without the franc improving on its own fundamentals.

catalysts.event: US September retail sales and PPI
catalysts.rationale: A strong consumption print keeps the real-yield channel open against a Swiss economy whose Q2 growth was half pharmaceuticals. It matters more for this pair than for most dollar crosses because the franc offers no growth story of its own to offset it.

catalysts.event: FOMC decision, no projections (gated meeting file, firm)
catalysts.rationale: The only scheduled policy decision for either currency inside the tactical window. October hike odds have fallen to roughly a fifth after the payrolls, so a hold is the base case. The tone on December determines whether the pair re-tests 0.8384. The differential can only hold or widen here.
The result sets the path to the 2026-12-11 funding deadline. Switzerland has no electoral counterpart inside either horizon, so the event exposure is one-sided on the base leg.

The second of the two prints that decide December SNB pricing, after September's 1.0%. A second reading at or above 1.0% validates the market's hike pricing and is the most likely route to a franc rally that needs no risk event.
After a 29,000 September print, a second sub-50,000 reading would take the December hike out of the price and remove the strategic base case's first condition.

catalysts.event: FOMC with Summary of Economic Projections (gated, firm)
catalysts.rationale: Delivery takes the differential to 412.5bp the day before the SNB speaks, and the 2027 dot sets the length of the Fed's plateau. The base leg sets the tone and the quote leg answers it 24 hours later.

catalysts.event: SNB quarterly assessment with conditional inflation forecast (gated, firm)
catalysts.rationale: The single largest binary in this analysis. A hold with a zero-rate forecast takes embedded hike premium out of the Swiss 2-year and supports the 0.8450 strategic base case. A hike or a normalisation reference inverts the largest input and targets 0.8000.

catalysts.event: Expiry of the US continuing resolution
catalysts.rationale: A shutdown at the year-end funding turn would revive the governance concerns Fitch flagged. It lands one day after the SNB, so the pair faces three consecutive days of one-sided dated risk, two of them on the base leg.

invalidators.condition: SNB hikes or references normalisation at the 2026-12-10 assessment, or the Swiss 2-year closes above 0.50% from 0.31%
invalidators.mechanism: That narrows the bilateral 2-year gap by about 20bp and converts the franc from the market's preferred funding currency into one with a tightening cycle ahead, which would force a concentrated −12.3%-of-open-interest short to cover.

invalidators.condition: US September core CPI on 2026-10-14 prints at or below 0.1% m/m and December hike odds fall below 40%
invalidators.mechanism: Combined with the 29,000 payroll print, that removes the base leg's only active driver while the franc's carry discount stays priced, so the pair loses its catalyst and ranges toward the 50-day at 0.81445.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Core CPI m/m; CME FedWatch December probability

invalidators.condition: The pair closes below 0.8184 (the 2026-09-22 higher low) and then below 0.8140 (the 50-day and the two-touch 0.81487–0.81620 shelf)
invalidators.mechanism: That breaks the higher-low sequence that has held since August and shows the crowded franc short covering faster than carry accrues, which is the pair-specific failure mode Factor 4 identifies.

invalidators.condition: OAT-Bund holds above 150bp for five sessions with EUR/CHF below 0.9300
invalidators.mechanism: A European sovereign event bids the franc through repatriation while doing nothing for the dollar's funding bid, which is the one haven configuration in which this haven-versus-haven pair falls cleanly.

invalidators.condition: Gold rises more than 8% in a month while the pair falls below 0.8235
invalidators.mechanism: Gold is the only commodity that moves both legs in the same direction (minus 0.53 correlation to the dollar, a shared haven bid for the franc), so a gold surge is the most reliable cross-asset sign that the pair's carry regime has broken.

invalidators.condition: The pair closes a week below 0.8000 (the top of the six-touch 0.79288–0.80001 floor)
invalidators.mechanism: That would put spot below both six-touch support bands and the 200-day, at which point six months of carry (about 160 pips) no longer covers the structural loss, and the external-balance factor's cap would have become a reversal.

invalidators.condition: CFTC leveraged-fund CHF positioning narrows beyond −4% of open interest from −12.3% while the pair is below 0.8200
invalidators.mechanism: That would show the covering flow has run its course into falling prices, which removes the funding leg rather than recycling it, and on this cross the funding leg is the trade.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: CFTC leveraged-fund CHF net / open interest

signposts.confirms_if: Widens above 460bp into the December cluster
signposts.bilateral_importance: It isolates the policy-expectation channel for both legs at once. The two policy rates are fixed until December, so this spread is the only live measure of whether the carry is widening or eroding.
It is the market's own measure of how much protection carry holders are buying against this specific cross, which neither currency's dossier skew can show.

signposts.confirms_if: Stable between −8% and −14% with the pair above 0.8235
signposts.invalidates_if: Narrows above −4%, or extends below −16% (dangerously crowded)
signposts.bilateral_importance: The franc is the funding leg of this cross specifically. ING and Reuters both document carry funding rotating from yen into franc and being expressed through USD/CHF.

signposts.current_level: 111.2bp at 2026-09-29; briefly above 150bp after the valuation date
signposts.bilateral_importance: A European credit event bids the franc and not the dollar, so it is the haven shock that hurts this pair most cleanly of all dollar crosses.

signposts.invalidates_if: Up more than 8% in a month
signposts.bilateral_importance: The pair's dominant commodity driver. It is the only commodity that moves both legs in the same direction.
The higher-low and 52-week-high pivots of this cross. They bracket the post-payroll consolidation.

assumptions: Price series, quoted verbatim from the payload: dataPoints 130; dateRange '2026-04-06 to 2026-10-02'; spot 0.8288; spotDate '2026-10-02'; computationRange '2007-11-30 to 2026-10-02 (4915 weekday bars)'; dataQuality 'USD/CHF: 4915 weekday bars in the store (2007-11-30 to 2026-10-02); 1007 weekly, 461 monthly; 130 daily bars passed downstream (2026-04-06 to 2026-10-02), which is the 1-6 month strategic horizon'; weekendBarsDropped 0.

Spot date. spotDate is one session after the 2026-10-01 valuation date, not before it. Every level, pip distance and percentage in this report is computed against 0.8288. No web spot was substituted. Web-reported intraday extremes (0.8382 high, 0.8225 low) differ slightly from the payload's 0.83836 and 0.82308, and the payload is used throughout. The CHF dossier's 0.83375 (2026-09-29) and the USD dossier's 0.8311 reference are superseded.

Price-derived metrics. Moving averages are simple averages of trading-day closes. Realised volatility is annualised on 252 days. ATR(14) is 54 pips. Zone distances in the zone table follow the payload convention (distance to zone midpoint); nearest-edge distances are the analyst's arithmetic. The 52-week percentile quoted in prose is the close-basis 90; the intraday-basis figure is 88.

200-week projection. The end-March 2027 level of about 0.842–0.845 is the analyst's estimate, not a payload figure. It assumes the weekly slope decays from −0.00087 as the late-2022 observations near 1.00 and the early-2023 observations near 0.92–0.94 (visible in the payload's zone members) roll out of the window. A linear extrapolation of the current slope would give about 0.834. The CHF dossier's statement of about 23 pips a quarter appears to understate the slope: −0.00087 a week is about 113 pips a quarter.
Yields. The payload's yield10y values (USD 4.68%, CHF 0.47%) are monthly series as of 2026-08-01 and are not quoted as live levels. Live long-end and 2-year references come from the dossiers.

Vol, carry and forwards. Implied volatility, risk reversals and butterflies are the payload's CME surface observed 2026-09-30. The 3-month figure is measured at 99.7 days. The implied-volatility percentile is not measurable from the payload; the CHF dossier's 35 is an estimate on an earlier observation. Forward points are derived linearly from the payload's −453.6bp futures roll, which embeds basis and cannot be separated from the rate differential. A policy-differential version is shown alongside.

Settled verdict. Factor stances, confidences, evidence types, weights, weighted contributions, net scores, convictions, rationales, score interpretations, rankings, consensus text and cross-horizon text are carried verbatim from pass 1. Pass-2 notes record where the analyst thinks post-valuation information weakens the tactical call. They do not change any score.

Post-valuation information. The US September payrolls (2026-10-02), the CME FedWatch repricing and the OAT-Bund move above 150bp were all published after the 2026-10-01 valuation date. They are used for levels, invalidator calibration and the analyst note only. The Swiss September CPI of 1.0% is as recorded in pass 1.

Trade inputs. Bilateral trade is the supplied IMF DOTS 2024 block, used without re-estimation. Trade-construction sizing uses a risk-budget convention (50bp of NAV at conviction 3, 30bp at conviction 2). It is illustrative and not specific to any account.
